hints.title: Root-to-Leaf Path Accumulation Obstacle
hints.text: A valid path must start at the root and terminate strictly at a leaf node while accumulating the exact target sum. How can tracking the path of visited nodes during traversal collect all matching paths?

hints.title: Backtracking Path Invariant
hints.text: Append each node to the current path buffer and subtract its value from targetSum. If reaching a leaf when remainder equals node value, record a copy of the path.

hints.title: Recursive Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: Use recursion passing current node, remaining target, and path accumulator. At each node, append node.val to path. If at a leaf and remaining sum equals node.val, append a copy of path to results. Recurse left and right with remaining sum - node.val. Pop the current node from path before returning.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Visiting each node once in O(N) with O(N) path copying for matching leaves (at most N/2 leaves).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Creating new path lists at every recursive call allocates excessive intermediate memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place path buffer with backtracking pop uses O(H) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using backtracking with append and pop on a single path list rather than creating list slices.
